newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen gets $97 mln loans from World Bank this year.
newsitem.headline: Yemen gets $97 mln loans from World Bank this year.

text.p: The World Bank's International Development Agency (IDA) has extended around $97 million in new loans to Yemen so far this year, the official Yemeni news agency Saba said on Tuesday.
"New loans provided by the IDA for Yemen this year are estimated at $97 million and will be used during the coming period in implementing different development projects," it said.
Between January and September this year Yemen has withdrawn about $88 million -- "a matter which reflects the improvement of competence level of the implementation of projects," Saba said.
The World Bank had complained that Yemen has been slow in implementing projects financed through soft loans it provides to the poor Arab state.
"The total loans provided by the IDA for projects being implemented in different sectors are estimated at $483 million...$237 million have been used already during the past period," it added.
Yemeni authorities and a World Bank delegation began their annual meeting in Sanaa on Monday.

The Bank's director for the Middle East and North Africa, Inder Sud is expected to hold a news conference in Sanaa on Wednesday to "shed light on progress achieved and competence recorded on the implementation of projects financed by the Bank," a Yemeni official said.

Yemen, where annual inflation is around 100 percent and unemployment is put at around 25 percent, is implementing an economic, financial and administrative reform programme agreed by the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
The IDA makes interest-free loans to poor countries.
